title: Lagged productivity and next-year real output in BLS detailed U.S. service industries
scope: 28 non-overlapping 2017 NAICS detailed industry codes, 2022–2025 archival table 1 snapshots
question: Does preceding-year output-per-hour growth help predict next-year real output growth, beyond the preceding year's real output growth alone?
primary_outcome: Annual percent change in real sectoral output for industry i year t
primary_metric: Holdout RMSE in percentage points, 2025, across all 28 industries

input_features.a_lag: Previous-year BLS labor_productivity_pct (real output per hour); measured/derived, not an exogenous technology shock

secondary_analysis.hours_forecast_identity: hhat_t = 100*((1+qhat_t/100)/(1+ahat_t/100)-1), using only predicted qhat and ahat; compare observed BLS total_hours_pct of 2025
secondary_analysis.benchmark: Simple hours growth persistence hhat_t = h_(t-1)
secondary_analysis.purpose: Evaluate actual labor-hours prediction, not validate the identity q=a*h (which is tautological).

uncertainty: Block-resample detailed industries, fixed fitted predictions, 2000 draws, deterministic seed 20261018; descriptive only, not an independent-population causal confidence interval
limitations: 2022-2025 tables are as-published different vintages, which may not be consistent revised timeseries.
2023 archived news release has corrections to table 2 and 3, only table 1 used.
Each preceding-year table was published mid-next-year; this is not a real-time January 1 forecast.
Four annual observations per 28 industries cannot robustly infer an AI structural break or separate business cycles.
No AI adoption metric at the same 2017 NAICS detail and annual frequency before 2025; none enters the regression.
Different industry sizes and shared macro shocks; estimates not population weighted.
Real output is production, not independently measured final customer demand; productivity is output/hours by construction.
Historical percent changes are rounded; the hours forecast is calculated from forecast q and a, not contemporaneous observed q and a.
